facts.statement: Spicomellus afer is the oldest named definitive ankylosaur dinosaur.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Spicomellus afer, representing the oldest named definitive ankylosaur.

facts.statement: Spicomellus afer was described in 2021 by Maidment and colleagues based on a single rib fragment fused to an osteoderm.
facts.quote: In 2021, Maidment and colleagues described Spicomellus afer as a new genus and species of ankylosaurian dinosaurs based on this specimen, accessioned as NHMUK PV R 37412.

facts.statement: The genus name Spicomellus combines the Latin words for 'spike' and 'collar'.
facts.quote: The generic name, Spicomellus, combines the Latin words spica, meaning "spike", and mellum, which refers to a collar.

facts.statement: A second specimen of Spicomellus was described in 2025 and accessioned at Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University.
facts.quote: In 2025, Maidment and colleagues described this second specimen, accessioned at Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University as specimens USMBA 5–84.

facts.statement: Several Spicomellus bones have been illegally excavated from Morocco and sold online.
facts.quote: Several Spicomellus bones have been illegally excavated and exported from Morocco, and then sold online.

facts.statement: Spicomellus is the only known vertebrate with dermal spikes fused directly to the bone.
facts.quote: The preserved dermal spikes of the holotype rib are fused directly to the bone, a trait unique to Spicomellus and not known from any other vertebrate.

facts.statement: Fused 'handle vertebrae' with ossified tendons in the tail of Spicomellus likely indicate the presence of a tail weapon.
facts.quote: Fused 'handle vertebrae' with associated ossified tendons are known from the tail of Spicomellus, which likely indicate it had a tail weapon.

facts.statement: The largest and most complete spike of Spicomellus is 87 cm long.
facts.quote: The largest and most complete spike is 87 cm long.

facts.statement: Spicomellus lived during the Bathonian age of the Middle Jurassic in Morocco.
facts.quote: Spicomellus is an extinct genus of unusual early ankylosaurian dinosaur from the El Mers III Formation (Bathonian age) of Morocco.

facts.statement: Spicomellus lived in Morocco, which was part of the supercontinent Gondwana during the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Spicomellus is known from the El Mers III Formation (El Mers Group) of Morocco. This would have been part of the supercontinent Gondwana during the Middle Jurassic.

facts.statement: Spicomellus indicates that ankylosaurs and stegosaurs coexisted for more than 20 million years.
facts.quote: The presence of the ankylosaur Spicomellus in addition to these genera indicates that the two major thyreophoran groups (Ankylosauria and Stegosauria) coexisted for more than 20 million years.

facts.statement: Spicomellus is assigned to the clade Eurypoda based on the T-shaped cross section of its ribs.
facts.quote: Based on the T-shaped cross section of the rib, Spicomellus can reasonably be assigned to the Eurypoda (the clade including stegosaurs and ankylosaurs, all of which bear T-shaped ribs).

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Spicomellus in an early-diverging clade within Ankylosauria outside of Ankylosauridae or Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: In their strict reduced consensus tree (shown below in Topology A), they recovered Spicomellus in an early-diverging clade within the Ankylosauria outside of either the Ankylosauridae or Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Using extended implied weights, Spicomellus was recovered as a basal member of Ankylosauridae, sister to Gobisaurus and Shamosaurus.
facts.quote: Using extended implied weights (shown below in Topology B), they instead recovered Spicomellus in a basal position within the family Ankylosauridae, as the sister taxon to the clade formed by Gobisaurus and Shamosaurus.

facts.statement: Spicomellus is the only known species in the extinct genus Spicomellus.
facts.quote: Spicomellus afer es la única especie conocida del género extinto Spicomellus

facts.statement: Spicomellus lived during the Middle Jurassic, between the Bathonian and Callovian stages, approximately 168 to 164 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico entre el Bathoniense y el Calloviense hace aproximadamente desde 168 a 164 millones de años

facts.statement: Spicomellus lived in what is now Africa.

facts.statement: Spicomellus was named and described in 2021.
facts.quote: nombrado y descrito en 2021

facts.statement: Spicomellus was likely similar in size to other Middle Jurassic ankylosaurs like Sarcolestes and Tianchiasaurus.
facts.quote: probablemente sea comparable en medida a otros anquilosaurios del Jurásico Medio, como Sarcolestes y Tianchiasaurus

facts.statement: The best estimates for the length of an adult Spicomellus are no more than 3 meters.

facts.statement: The preserved dermal spines of the holotype were fused to the bone.
facts.quote: las espinas dermales preservadas del holotipo se habían fusionado con el hueso

facts.statement: Because its dorsal spines were fused to the bone rather than attached to muscle tissue like in other ankylosaurs, this trait likely made movement difficult for Spicomellus.

facts.statement: The fused T-shaped rib with spines is a unique characteristic of Spicomellus and is unknown in any other vertebrate.

facts.statement: Remains of Spicomellus were found in the third subunit of the El Mers Group, dated to the Middle Jurassic, near Boulahfa, south of Boulemane, Fès-Meknès, Morocco.

facts.statement: Spicomellus afer was described by Maidment et al. on September 23, 2021, in an online article in the paleontological journal Nature Ecology & Evolution.

facts.statement: Spicomellus likely had a close relationship to the only other known ankylosaurs of the time, the genera Sarcolestes from the UK and Tianchisaurus from China.

facts.statement: Spicomellus is the second described eurypod taxon from North Africa, after Adratiklit.

facts.statement: Spicomellus is the oldest known ankylosaur in the world, with the possible exception of an unnamed thyreophoran from the Isle of Skye, Scotland, which could be up to 2 million years older.

facts.statement: The predators in the ecosystem consisted of indeterminate theropods, possibly megalosaurids.

facts.statement: The discovery of Spicomellus shows that Ankylosauria and Stegosauria coexisted for over 20 million years, implying that stegosaur extinction was caused by other unknown reasons, contradicting the traditional belief that they were displaced by ankylosaurs.
